To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
focal cerebral ischemia causes a rapid and transient increase in brain content of serum proteins (66 and 80kDa) in the ischemic penumbra, which are probably derived from the plasma.
the 66 kD protein (albumin) and 80 kD protein (transferrrin) are increased in ischemic tissue, while the 260 kD protein (unidentified) is reduced.

(i) Focal ischemia induced significant changes in the brain content and localization of serum proteins; (ii) Albumin and transferrin, the 66 and the 80 kDa bands, respectively, were increased in the ischemic brain; (iii) The 260 kDa band was decreased in the ischemic cerebral cortex and para-ischemia hippocampus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the biochemical changes that occur following MCAO in rat.
the early effects of permanent focal cerebral ischemia on the content of serum and plasma proteins in the ischemic hemisphere and the penumbra.
the identification of proteins that change their content in the brain after ischemic injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 66, 80 and 260 kD proteins may be considered as markers for ischemic brain tissue.
these proteins may be involved in the pathogenesis of cerebral ischemia.
the 260 kD band represents a protein that is not present in the plasma, but is present in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain proteins are affected by ischemic insult, and the changes in their levels and distribution may reflect the pathophysiologic processes that occur in focal cerebral ischemia.
the brain is not an isolated organ and the blood-brain barrier is not an absolute barrier to plasma proteins.
the brain proteins are affected by focal ischemia and that the alteration in the content of these proteins may be related to the pathogenesis of ischemic brain damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the proteins that are affected by focal ischemia.
the 260 kD protein was decreased in ischemic and para ischemic tissues, while the 80 and 66 kD proteins were increased in the ischemic hemisphere.
the 66 kD and 80 kD proteins are related to serum albumin and serum transferrin, respectively, and their increase in the ischemic brain may be due to their leakage from the blood vessels.
